group_assessment.weighting: The Chang laboratory (Guthrie Research Institute and National Cheng Kung University, from the affiliations) that cloned Zfra and WOX1-binding partners and wrote most of the WWOX apoptosis and Tyr33 literature. Primary for WWOX stress signalling in cultured cells; not a WWOX loss-of-function, neurological or metabolic group. Observation (cell-death percentages, blots) weighed above the pathway cartoon of Figure 12, which the paper itself marks as unvalidated.

entries.proposition: The paper measures no mitochondrial event; its statement that the Zfra/WOX1 complex co-translocates to mitochondria is attributed to a manuscript then submitted by the same group.
entries.snippet: the Zfra/WOX1 complex co-translocates to the mitochondria to regulate cell death via the mitochondrial pathway (Hsu et al., submitted)

entries.proposition: Every perturbation is an overexpression of Zfra, mouse WOX1 or a point mutant in cultured cell lines; the cells that die include Zfra-negative lines, so cell death is not tied to endogenous Zfra or WWOX.
entries.snippet: Following 48 hr in culture, Zfra induced death of human cell lines including ovarian ME180, embryonic kidney HEK-293, neuroblastoma SK-N-SH, Molt4 T lymphocytes, and breast MCF7 and MDA-MB-231 cells, and murine L929 fibroblasts (Figure 1A).
entries.anchor: Results, Transiently overexpressed Zfra induces apoptosis

entries.proposition: In the yeast two-hybrid assay a Tyr33-to-Arg substitution abolishes Zfra binding to the WW domain; this tests the residue, and the text infers that phosphorylation is required although phosphorylation is not measured in yeast.
entries.snippet: Alteration of the known phosphorylation site Tyr33 to Arg in this domain abrogated the binding (Figure 6), suggesting that Tyr33 phosphorylation is needed for WOX1 to interact with Zfra.
entries.anchor: Results, Zfra physically interacts with TRADD, and binds to the N-terminal first WW domain and C-terminal SDR domain of WOX1

entries.proposition: Zfra binds the SDR domain but not the mitochondria-targeting region inside it, so the binding site for Zfra is not the region that targets WOX1 to mitochondria.
entries.snippet: Zfra also bound the C-terminal SDR domain. This domain has a mitochondria-targeting region, and Zfra did not bind to this region (Figure 6).
entries.anchor: Results, Zfra physically interacts with TRADD, and binds to the N-terminal first WW domain and C-terminal SDR domain of WOX1

entries.proposition: Overexpressed Zfra keeps WOX1, p53, NF-kappaB and p-ERK out of the nucleus in SK-N-SH cells; the readout is a cytosol and nucleus fractionation blot, not a mitochondrial fraction.
entries.snippet: Transiently overexpressed EGFP-Zfra suppressed nuclear localization of NF-κB (p65), WOX1, p53, p-ERK (extracellular signal-regulated kinase), but had little or no effect on JNK1/2 (Figure 8A).
entries.anchor: Results, Transiently overexpressed Zfra sequesters WOX1, NF-kB, p53 and p-ERK in the cytoplasm

entries.snippet: TNF increased the binding of GST-Zfra with JNK1, NF-κB (p65) and p-WOX1 (Tyr33 phosphorylated), and weakly with p53 in a time-related manner (Figure 7B and 7C).

entries.proposition: Zfra and WOX1 given together do not add up in cell death; the paper reads this as mutual counteraction.
entries.snippet: However, when in combination, Zfra and WOX1 failed to synergistically increase cell death (Figure 9C).
entries.anchor: Results, Zfra counteracts the apoptotic function of WOX1

entries.proposition: The SDR domain alone does not kill cells and gains no effect from Zfra; only SDR plus the C-terminal tail does, so no enzymatic readout of the SDR domain exists in this paper.
entries.snippet: SDR alone could not cause cell death and Zfra and SDR, in combination, did not increase the cell death (Figure 10C).
entries.anchor: Results, Phosphorylation at Tyr33 is essential for WOX1 to counteract Zfra-mediated apoptosis
